verdict.rationale: Microsoft's first-party Graph mail docs show the product's own search capability: filtering, searching and sorting across folders or the entire mailbox, OData query parameters, and search folders. That evidence is API-level, not the end-user search box, and one hands-on user found searching via an LLM integration faster than Outlook's web search field. missing for 10: documented search operators/syntax in the client UI, ranked/relevance-ordered results, evidence of speed and precision across full history, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, search is fast and precise — operators, filters, and ranked results across my full mail history

citations.quote: Apps can conveniently [filter, search, or sort](query-parameters) messages in specific folders or the user's entire mailbox.
Query for messages and get them in a search folder
Apps can control the behavior of GET requests by using [OData query parameters](/en-us/graph/query-parameters).
